newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland Bank supervisor confirms markka - ERM plan.
newsitem.headline: Finland Bank supervisor confirms markka - ERM plan.

text.p: Finland Bank supervisory board member Anneli Jaatteenmaki on Saturday confirmed the board had met on Friday and proposed to the government that the markka be linked to Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism.
"Yes, the meeting was held yesterday," she told Reuters by telephone. Asked what the central markka-ERM parity was, she said: "It is a secret decision."

Second finance minister Arja Alho made the proposal at an extraordinary session late on Friday night, Finnish radio said, adding that the supervisory board had voted by five to four in favour of the proposal.
Diplomats in Brussels said the European Union's monetary committee was meeting there on Saturday to discuss the markka's entry into the ERM.

The markka has been floating freely since September 8, 1992. It was briefly linked unilaterally to the European currency unit (Ecu) between June and November 1991, when it was devalued by around 12 percent and then re-linked to the Ecu.
Finland's five-party coalition government is determined to be among the first countries to join a European single currency.
The EU monetary committee is made up of national treasury and central bank officials. The markka was trading at 2.986 to the German mark at Friday's market close.
